bear.text: EBITDA margin contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1 FY27, down from 12.9% in the prior year period.
Management attributes the increase in receivable days from 78 to 96 over the last year mainly to slower payments from two large state utility customers.
The company received a GST demand order for ₹46.3 crore, including interest and penalty, relating to input tax credits claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.

bull.text: Revenue from operations increased 18.0% year-on-year to ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27.
The order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year earlier.
Management states the new Bharuch plant, which adds about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27.
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27, an increase from 16% in the same quarter of the previous year.

open_questions.text: The company's press release reports Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹1,248 crore, while a news article reports ₹1,428 crore. What explains this discrepancy between the official filing and the secondary report?
Management intends to appeal the ₹46.3 crore GST demand and states it does not expect a material impact on financial position. What is the current status of this appeal?

snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors listed on the NSE.
For the quarter ended 30 June 2026, the company reported revenue of ₹1,248 crore and profit after tax of ₹82 crore.
As of 30 June 2026, promoters and the promoter group held 58.2% of the company's shares.
The share of promoter holdings pledged with lenders was 4.1% as of 30 June 2026, down from 11.5% in June 2025.
